answer_1.quote: Faithfulness evaluation metrics are crucial for assessing the factual consistency of text generated by models relative to the source text. It receives great interest within the field of natural language generation (NLG) , particularly in abstractive summarization .
tasks: Other: retrieval-augmented LLMs for generative search
answer_1.outputs: statements with in-line citations generated by retrieval-augmented LLMs

answer_2.quote: Faithfulness evaluation metrics are employed as proxies to automatically estimate the citation support . These metrics measure the faithfulness between model-generated and sourced text, which aligns closely with the objectives of automated citation evaluation.

answer_3.quote: we introduce two prompting methods as follows: (i) Discrete scoring prompts the LLM to assign discrete scores from the set 0, 1, 2 for a given statement and its citation, where 1 indicates full support, 0 indicates no support, and values between 0 and 1 indicate partial support. (ii) Continuous scoring prompts the LLM to assign a continuous score from the range [0, 1] for a given statement and its citation.

answer_4.quote: For this benchmark, human assessors are enrolled to annotate each statement-citation pair based on the degree to which the citation supports the associated statement.
answer_4.guideline: We adopt the definition of these support levels from Liu et al. ( ): • Full Support (FS): the citation fully supports every detail in the statement. • Partial Support (PS): the citation supports certain aspects of the statement, while other details remain unsupported or are contradicted. • No Support (NS): none of the content in the statement is supported by the citation.
